source: B. F. Stevens (ed.), The Campaign in Virginia, 1781: An Exact Reprint of Six Rare Pamphlets on the Clinton-Cornwallis Controversy. With Very Numerous Important Unpublished Manuscript Notes (London, 1888), vol. 2
rights: public domain (possible-copyright-status NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT per archive.org metadata); University of Toronto / Robarts Library scan
fetch_method: archive.org /metadata for page_numbers.json (printed page -> leaf mapping), then direct zip-member fetch of the item's own _jp2.zip (https://archive.org/download/<id>/<id>_jp2.zip/<id>_jp2%2F<id>_<leaf>.jp2), converted to JPEG locally and downsized to 1400px wide for the repo; browser User-Agent, ~1.5-1.6s apart, 5 requests total (1 metadata + 4 leaves; page_numbers.json fetch is bundled in the metadata call's file list, fetched separately as a 5th request). AX-STEV2 (26 Sept 2026) located pages 146-147, 156-157, 172-173 the same way: vol.1's own djvu.txt (campaigninvirgin01stevuoft, the 'CHRONOLOGICAL CORRESPONDENCE' apparatus, not saved to the repo -- disk-only, 1 request) gave the 'see Letter ii. NNN' page pointers for items dated 31 Aug/16 Sept/30 Sept 1781; the +8 page-to-leaf offset confirmed unchanged at all three pairs (146+8=154, 156+8=164, 172+8=180); 6 more leaves fetched the same zip-member route, 6 requests, 1.5-1.6s apart.

images.shows: 16 Aug 1781, Cornwallis to Clinton (item 141B, = PRO 30/55/32/2, item 3689). Opening: 'Endorsed Duplicate. Earl Cornwallis to Sir H. Clinton K.B. York 16th August 1781 ... The Original was written in Cypher.' Letter body begins 'Duplicate York Town in Virginia 16 Augst 1781. Sir, This morning I received your Cyphered Letter of the 11th instant, by the Runner...' -- printed in clear English throughout this page, continues onto p.128.

Continuation and end of the 16 Aug 1781 letter (signed CORNWALLIS, addressed to Clinton), followed by the item-141 apparatus: '141B: CORNWALLIS to CLINTON, 16 August 1781, ANSWER [185] i.90 ... Same as No. 141 with variations shown in margins pp 127-128' and '141F: ... CORRESPONDENCE [24] i.135 ... Same as No. 141 with variations shown in margins pp 127-128' -- no cipher tag on either apparatus line itself; the cipher note sits only in the p.127 endorsement above.

3 Oct 1781, Cornwallis to Clinton (item 163, = PRO 30/55/33/7, item 3813). Apparatus header '163 CORNWALLIS to CLINTON, 3 October 1781, LS RI 19/138. ANSWER [201] i.92, CORRESPONDENCE [56] i.136, with Clinton's Manuscript Notes from each.' Endorsement: 'Lord Cornwallis to Sir H. Clinton K.B. 3d Octr 1781 recd 12th at 2 A.M. 228' -- no cipher word in this endorsement. Letter body begins 'York Town Virginia 3 Octr 1781. Sir, I received your Letter of the 25th of September, last night...' and continues onto p.175.

End of the 3 Oct 1781 letter. An asterisk in the body text (before the paragraph starting '* I can see no means of forming a junction with me but by York River...') marks the start of the ciphered passage; footnote below the signature block: '* [From here partly in cypher with a translation.]' -- i.e. only the final paragraph (French-fleet strength, junction, Capes) was in cipher in the manuscript, not the whole letter. Apparatus line below: '163B: CORNWALLIS to CLINTON, 3 October 1781, ANSWER [201] i.92 ... Earl Cornwallis to Sir Henry Clinton, dated York-Town, Virginia, October 3, 1781. [In Cypher.]' -- this is the TNA-matching cipher tag, attached to copy 163B specifically.

Item 149, CORNWALLIS to CLINTON, 31 August 1781 (= PRO 30/55/32/66, item 3753). 'Endorsed Duplicate. Earl Cornwallis to Sir H. Clinton, K.B., York August 31st 1781 recd the 4th Septr 1781...' Letter body printed in full: 'Sir, A French Ship of the Line, with two Frigates, & the Loyalist, which they have taken, lay at the Mouth of this River, A Lieutenant of the Charon, who went with an Escort of Dragoons to Old Point Comfort, reports, that there are* between 30 and 40 Sail within the Capes, mostly Ships of War, & some of them very large...' with footnote '* [From here in cypher with translation in margin]' after 'large' -- matches item 3753's TNA description verbatim ('A French ship of the line with two frigates and the Loyalist which they have taken, lay at the mouth of this river. A Lieutenant of the Charon who went w[ith]...'). Apparatus line '149B: Cornwallis to Clinton, 31 August 1781, ANSWER [189] i.91 ... Earl Cornwallis to Sir Henry Clinton, K.B. dated Yorktown, in Virginia, 31st August, 1781. [In Cypher.]'

Continuation of apparatus for item 149 (31 Aug 1781, = item 3753): further copy variants (149S/149V/149E/149R/149M), all '[In Cypher.]' or 'the same letter as No. 149', including the French translation sent to Germain. Then item 150, CORNWALLIS to CLINTON, 1 Sept. 1781 (a different, one-line note, not one of our 12 named items): 'An enemy's fleet within the Capes, between thirty and forty ships of war, mostly large. CORNWALLIS.' '[Written in Cypher on a Congress Note.]' -- unrelated to 3753/3784/3803, included only because it shares the leaf.

Item 156, CORNWALLIS to CLINTON, 16 Sept. 1781 (= PRO 30/55/32/97, item 3784). 'Endorsed Cypher Duplicate. Earl Cornwallis to Sir Henry Clinton 16th & 17th Septr 1781. received (Wednesday, per the Schooner Mary) Septr 27th 1781. Duplicate York Town Virginia, 16th Septr 1781.' Letter body begins 'Sir, I have received your Letters of the 2d & 6th. The Enemy's Fleet has returned. Two Line of Battle Ships, & one Frigate, lie at the mouth of this River; & three or four Line of Battle Ships, several Frigates' (continues onto p.157) -- matches item 3784's TNA description ('the enemy fleet has returned, two line of battle ships and one frigate lie at the mouth of this river, and three...') verbatim; header cites ANSWER [196] i.92, CORRESPONDENCE [52] i.136, REPLY [103] i.171.

End of the 16-17 Sept 1781 letter (item 3784): '...& Transports, went up the Bay on the 12th & 14th. I hear Washington arrived at Williamsburgh on the 14th... If I had no hopes of Relief, I would rather risk an Action than defend my half-finished Works. But as you say Admiral Digby is hourly expected, and promise every Exertion to assist me, I do not think myself justifiable in putting the fate of the War on so desperate an Attempt.' No cipher-transition footnote on this leaf (the endorsement on p.156 already marks the whole letter 'Cypher Duplicate'); printed in clear throughout. Followed by Clinton's manuscript-note apparatus (numbered footnotes 1-10) responding point by point, dated from his own later marginalia.

Item 162, CLINTON to CORNWALLIS, 30 Sept. 1781 (= PRO 30/55/32/116, item 3803). 'Sir Henry Clinton to Earl Cornwallis, dated New-York, September 30, 1781. [Duplicate, in Cypher.] [Received October 10, from Major Cockran.]' Letter body printed in full: 'My Lord, Your Lordship may be assured that I am doing every thing in my power to relieve you by a direct move, and I have reason to hope, from the assurances given me this day by Admiral Graves, that we may pass the bar by the 12th of October...' (continues onto p.173) -- matches item 3803's TNA description ('Clinton to Cornwallis. New York. Two copies of a document, the first in code. Assuring his lordship that he is doing everything in his power to relieve him by a direct move...') verbatim; header cites ANSWER [202] i.92, CORRESPONDENCE [55] i.136.

End of the 30 Sept 1781 letter (item 3803), signed 'H. CLINTON.' No cipher-transition footnote on this leaf; margin note on p.172 reads 'V in cypher to p 173 l 2' (variant V's manuscript is in cipher up to line 2 of p.173, i.e. almost the whole letter) -- printed text here is the full deciphered/clear text throughout. Followed by copy-variant apparatus (162B/162F/162S/162V/162E/162R), all '[In cypher]' or 'the same letter as No. 162', including one noting the printed heading was 'by mistake omitted in the printing' in some copies.
